(amongst other things!)
CI just needed some fixes from nightly-testing that hadn't made it in.
Review / triage particularly appreciated here, we have more backed up behind this one.

Reviewers may find the following script helpful:

Claude: can you please give me a one-line shell command that will mark as "viewed" on github all the files in https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4-nightly-testing/pull/215/changes whose only diff is adding lines of the form set_option backward.defeqAttrib.useBackward true in?

PR=215; R=leanprover-community/mathlib4-nightly-testing; ID=$(gh pr view $PR -R $R --json id -q .id); gh api --paginate "repos/$R/pulls/$PR/files" --jq '.[] | select(.patch != null) | select(.patch | split("\n") | map(select(test("^[+-]") and (test("^[+-]{3}") | not))) | (length > 0) and all(test("^\\+\\s*set_option backward\\.defeqAttrib\\.useBackward true in\\s*$"))) | .filename' | while IFS= read -r f; do gh api graphql -f query='mutation($pr:ID!,$p:String!){markFileAsViewed(input:{pullRequestId:$pr,path:$p}){pullRequest{id}}}' -F pr="$ID" -F p="$f" >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "OK: $f" || echo "FAIL: $f"; done
CI is now passing.

Hmm, https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4-nightly-testing/commit/eb6f701f5e9 doesn't quite look right to me: 

  if defeqAttr.hasTag (← getEnv) src then
    /- It can be that `src` holds reflexively but `tgt` doesn't, so we need to use `inferDefEqAttr`.
    For example in `Ici_inter_Iic : Ici a ∩ Iic b = Icc a b := rfl`. -/
    MetaM.run' <| inferDefEqAttr tgt
    /- Under the strict `@[defeq]` inference of lean4#13492, `inferDefEqAttr` tags the
    additive translation only `@[backward_defeq]` even when the multiplicative source is
    `@[defeq]` and the additive proof is rfl-shaped, because `withReducibleAndInstances`
    `isDefEq` checks fail systematically for `to_additive`-generated additive lemmas
    (the additive instance projections don't reduce at instance transparency).
    To keep the simp/dsimp behaviour symmetric between additive and multiplicative
    versions, promote `tgt` to `@[defeq]` whenever the source is `@[defeq]` and the
    translated proof is at least rfl-shaped (i.e. `@[backward_defeq]` was inferred). -/
    if backwardDefeqAttr.hasTag (← getEnv) tgt && !defeqAttr.hasTag (← getEnv) tgt then
      defeqAttr.setTag tgt

The code is only reachable if the original theorem is [defeq], but if the original theorem is only [backward_defeq], nothing happens.

On the adaption branch for lean4#13557 Claude wrote

  if defeqAttr.hasTag (← getEnv) src || backwardDefeqAttr.hasTag (← getEnv) src then
    /- It can be that `src` holds reflexively but `tgt` doesn't, so we need to use `inferDefEqAttr`.
    For example in `Ici_inter_Iic : Ici a ∩ Iic b = Icc a b := rfl`.
    We also propagate `backward_defeq`: theorems auto-tagged because they are `:= rfl` and
    used under `set_option backward.defeqAttrib.useBackward true` need their additive
    counterparts to have the same tag, otherwise the `useBackward` escape hatch breaks
    when proofs that worked on the multiplicative version are translated. -/
    MetaM.run' <| inferDefEqAttr tgt

which also doesn’t seem to be quite right: Here the src tags don't matter.

Probably the right behaviour is:

  • If src has [defeq] and tgt can have [defeq], make it so
  • If src has [backward_defeq] and tgt can have [backward_defeq], make it so
  • Have a trace option that tells you when the attribute could not be transferred (this can happen, as menitoned in that comment)

That is now at https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4-nightly-testing/commit/ac6ba8a38970ef5319e786067e90ea3b2558f5ac. I assume it makes sense to cherry-pick that onto nightly-testing and also nightly#215?

This may be an interesting find:

to_app macro silently depends on useBackward (lean4#13557 adaptation)

While migrating Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Bicategory/Strict/Pseudofunctor.lean away
from set_option backward.defeqAttrib.useBackward true, several _app /
_app_assoc lemmas generated by @[to_app] started producing subtly different
types — types that print identically but whose hashes differ, breaking
downstream rfl arguments in e.g. IsPrestack.overMapCompPresheafHomIso and
DescentData.

Root cause: to_app builds the _app form via simpType catAppSimp ….
catAppSimp (in Mathlib/Tactic/CategoryTheory/ToApp.lean) is a simpOnlyNames
call with 17 lemmas; four of them are tagged [backward_defeq] only:
Cat.Hom.comp_toFunctor, Functor.comp_obj, Cat.Hom₂.comp_app, eqToHom_refl.
With useBackward = true in scope, simp lets these lemmas fire
without, the simp output ends up with a different proof shape and a less-reduced type.

The four lemmas can't simply be promoted to [defeq] — they genuinely fail the
instance-transparency check ((F ≫ G).toFunctor vs F.toFunctor ⋙ G.toFunctor
needs default/all transparency to unfold Cat.bicategory.comp / Functor.comp).

Workaround used: keep set_option backward.defeqAttrib.useBackward true in
on the affected to_app declarations (5 in Pseudofunctor.lean, with adaptation
notes pointing back at lean4#13557).

This seems to fit in with the issues described in #general > backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency @ 💬. So the plan would be to change things so that these lemmas can again be tagged with [defeq].

So I would actually suggest as a workaround to use set_option backward.defeqAttrib.useBackward true in the implementation of to_app.

Claude also suggested that; seemed to be a bit too much under the rag for me, but it’s up to you.

Not all the lemmas applied by catAppSimp are [defeq] (even before all this). Is it desirable that this simplification is not either all-dsimp (rewrites consistently everywhere) or all non-defeq (rewrites only in non-dependent positions)? But that’s probably a distraction.

Claude tried but

The change to to_app is too broad — it changes the shape of all _app/_app_assoc lemmas
across mathlib (since they all now get re-elaborated under useBackward=true), breaking
downstream proofs that rely on the less-reduced form. Reverting
I didn't mean to elaborate anything under useBackward=true, I meant to just run the simp only with that option.

I think that’s what Claude tried

--- a/Mathlib/Tactic/CategoryTheory/ToApp.lean
+++ b/Mathlib/Tactic/CategoryTheory/ToApp.lean
@@ -138,6 +138,12 @@ initialize registerBuiltinAttribute {
   | `(attr| to_app $optAttr) => MetaM.run' do
     if (kind != AttributeKind.global) then
       throwError "`to_app` can only be used as a global attribute"
+    -- `catAppSimp` rewrites with several `[backward_defeq]`-only lemmas (e.g.
+    -- `Cat.Hom.comp_toFunctor`, `Functor.comp_obj`); without `useBackward true`,
+    -- those lemmas don't fire and the generated `_app` lemma's type is less reduced,
+    -- breaking downstream `rfl` arguments. Set the option here so callers don't have
+    -- to scatter `set_option backward.defeqAttrib.useBackward true in` annotations.
+    withOptions (·.setBool `backward.defeqAttrib.useBackward true) do
     addRelatedDecl src (src.appendAfter "_app") ref optAttr fun value levels => do
       let levelMVars ← levels.mapM fun _ => mkFreshLevelMVar
       let value := value.instantiateLevelParams levels levelMVars

Hmm, I guess that while these things that we want to be implicitly reducible are not implicitly reducible, things will break when we make changes. I just thought that we'd need less of the backward options if we did it like this.
Assuming the goal is to get rid of them eventually it’s probably better to have more slective ones than a single broad one.

Joachim Breitner said:

Is it desirable that this simplification is not either all-dsimp (rewrites consistently everywhere) or all non-defeq

Ah, it could be that it is desirable to not rewrite in dependent positions in this simp only, in which case it makes sense not to use useBackward=true.
If that is desirable , maybe set (dsimp := false) in the simp config. That would certainly make this feature more robust against [defeq] changes

Ok, so I've run into an issue: when adding @[to_app] to docs#CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor.mapComp'_inv_whiskerRight_mapComp'₀₂₃_inv,

@[to_app]
lemma mapComp'_inv_whiskerRight_mapComp'₀₂₃_inv (hf : f₀₂ ≫ f₂₃ = f) :
    (F.mapComp' f₀₁ f₁₂ f₀₂ h₀₂).inv ▷ F.map f₂₃ ≫ (F.mapComp' f₀₂ f₂₃ f).inv =
    (α_ _ _ _).hom ≫ F.map f₀₁ ◁ (F.mapComp' f₁₂ f₂₃ f₁₃ h₁₃).inv ≫
      (F.mapComp' f₀₁ f₁₃ f).inv

The Bicategory.associator, α_, (which is "equal" to the identity morphism) currently disappears in the to_app version. It seems a bit inconsistent that we abuse definitonal equality in the app version, but not in the original. @Robin Carlier do you know if this is intentional and what the reasoning for this is?
(Maybe worth moving the dicussion about to_app to its own thread?)
